newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PUBLIC WAGES 18 PCT HIGHER THAN PRIVATE-GUS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PUBLIC WAGES 18 PCT HIGHER THAN PRIVATE-GUS.

text.p: Polish workers employed in the public sector earn 18 percent more than those employed in the private sector, the Central Statistic Office (GUS) said in a report presented to journalists on Friday.
It said however, emploeeys with higher education earned more money in the private sector than in the public sector.

"Wages for graduates are higher in the private sector than in the public sector... but on average earnings in the public sector are 18 percent higher than those in private firms," said Malgorzata Kolaska, head of the GUS' labour department.

In March 1996, when the report was prepared, the average wage in public sector was 897 zlotys and in private sector 758 zlotys, but graduates in private sector earned 1523 zlotys on average against public sector's 1156 zlotys.
The report said that regardless of the sector men's wages were 26.2 percent higher on average then womens'.
